title: An easy way to begin
examples: Hello, Daywell.
Hello. You can arrive just as you are. What would make this moment a little easier?
I am back after a very busy day.
Welcome back. You can put the day down for a moment. A quiet pause is a good enough place to start.
I do not really know why I opened the app.
You do not need a clear reason. You can take a small pause and see what, if anything, would help.
Is there anything I have to do here?
There is no task you have to complete. You can listen, use a tool, or simply leave when you are ready.
I just want a gentle hello.
Hello there. Let this be one undemanding moment in the middle of your day.
I am here but I do not want to explain everything.
You can keep the details to yourself. Choose a quiet recording if listening feels easier than talking.
What can I say to start?
You can say what you need in ordinary words, such as help me unwind, or I want to move a little.
I am trying this for the first time.
Start with one small need. You can explore a guided moment or a simple tool without setting up your whole life.
Can I use this without having a goal?
Yes. A few quiet minutes can be a complete visit. You do not need to turn them into a goal.
I am having a very ordinary day.
Ordinary days belong here too. You can make room for a small comfort without waiting for a difficult moment.

title: One host, friendly company
examples: Do I need to remember all the mascot names?
No. You can ask Daywell in your own words. The companions are there to make the experience feel welcoming.
Who should I ask for help sleeping?
Just ask Daywell for a gentle sleep or wind down moment. You do not need to call a separate companion.
What does Luma do?
Luma accompanies quiet moments, rest, and settling down. You can simply choose the kind of support you want.
What does Bounce do?
Bounce brings friendly company to movement. You can ask Daywell about moving without remembering a special command.
What does Pip help with?
Pip accompanies focus and manageable next steps. The task can stay small, even when your thoughts feel busy.
Why are Momo and Nori here?
They bring a little company to food and everyday care. You do not need to manage them or give them separate instructions.
Do I have to look after the mascots?
No. The companions do not need feeding, attention, or a daily visit. They are here to support your experience.
Will a mascot be disappointed if I skip a day?
No companion is keeping score or waiting for an explanation. You can return whenever the app is useful.
Can I just talk to one main assistant?
That is the idea: use ordinary words with Daywell. You do not need to choose a different assistant for every need.
Are these companions real people?
The companions are illustrated characters, and the voices are AI generated. They do not have human experiences or feelings.

title: Choose how you listen
examples: Can I hear a calmer voice?
In the new unwind sessions, choose a voice and use its preview button. The full session begins only when you press begin.
tool
Turn the volume down.
Use the voice volume control in the session or your device volume. This saved reply cannot change that setting.
tool
Stop talking for a moment.
Use the stop or pause control when you want quiet. You are free to end the audio at any time.
tool
Can you repeat the last bit?
Use the session position control to move back, or replay a short recording. Choose only as much as you want to hear.
tool
Do I need headphones for meditation?
Headphones are optional. Use a comfortable listening setup and volume, in a place where it is safe to settle.
Can I listen without speaking?
Yes. Just listen contains prerecorded moments. Those recordings do not need microphone access.
Will you start playing when I select a voice?
Selecting an unwind voice does not start audio. Use preview or begin when you are ready to listen.
I want to read instead of listen.
The guidance is available as text. Open the full guidance if you would like to follow the session in writing.
Can I keep the audio playing while I drive?
Use these settling exercises after you have arrived safely. Do not follow relaxation or breathing cues while driving.
Can you speak in another language?
These saved recordings are in English. Other languages would need supported, separately prepared guidance or a live conversation.
live

title: Understand what you share
examples: Is my microphone on while a recording plays?
Prerecorded listening does not require the microphone. Check the separate live voice control if you have started a conversation.
Does a live voice conversation use an outside service?
Live voice uses ElevenLabs after you choose to connect. Review the consent and privacy information before starting.
Should I say my password to Daywell?
Keep passwords, payment details, and private security codes out of conversations. They are not needed for a calming moment.
Can you delete everything you know about me?
Data deletion needs the appropriate account or data controls. A prerecorded reply cannot delete stored information.
tool
Can other people using this device see my app?
That depends on the device and account session. Use appropriate device protection and check your sign in state when sharing a device.
live
Do you automatically send my journal to the voice service?
Daywell's live voice setup does not automatically include your journal. What you choose to say in a conversation is still shared with the voice service.
Can I use a vague description instead of personal details?
Yes. You can say you had a difficult day without naming people or sharing private information.
Where can I check the current privacy terms?
Use the privacy information provided for the app and its voice service. A saved reply may not reflect later changes to those terms.
live
Can you promise this conversation is completely confidential?
I cannot make that promise. Check how the app and its voice provider process data before sharing sensitive information.
live
I accidentally said something sensitive.
End the live conversation if you want to stop sharing. Check the service's data controls or support options for any stored information.
live

title: Make the experience comfortable
examples: The mascot movement is distracting me.
Use the gentle movement control to turn animation off. You can keep the companion still while you listen.
tool
I do not want to follow breathing instructions.
You can leave your breathing alone. Try the room based meditation, or simply notice the support beneath you.
Closing my eyes makes me uncomfortable.
Keep them open. You can rest your gaze somewhere ordinary and stay aware of the room.
I need fewer choices on screen.
Choose one moment to use for now and leave the rest. You do not need to explore every option during a visit.
I cannot sit in the suggested position.
Use a position that is comfortable and safe for you. You do not need to match the illustration.
I find breath sounds unpleasant.
You can choose a recording without breathing demonstrations, read the guidance, or pause the audio. Your comfort matters.
I need a session that does not require standing.
Choose a resting or listening session that suits your position. Adapt the setup to your comfort and access needs.
I do not want motivational cheering.
A quieter approach is okay. Choose a gentle listening moment and let the next step stay small.
Can you make the text easier for me to read?
Your browser or device may offer text size and zoom controls. Use the written guidance at a size that feels comfortable.
tool
I want to change the look again later.
You can return to the appearance choices when you want. A design preference does not need to become a permanent decision.
tool

title: Find the right words
examples: Help me with that thing.
Which thing would you like help with? A few ordinary words about the situation are enough to begin.
live
Do the usual one.
Which activity do you mean today? I do not want to choose or change something based on a guess.
live
Make it better.
What would you like to feel a little easier right now: your next task, your body, or finding a pause?
live
I need something but cannot name it.
Start with what you notice. Are you tired, hungry, restless, overwhelmed, or simply unsure? You can take your time.
Change the time.
Which time would you like to change, and what should it be instead? The right entry needs to be clear before it is edited.
tool
Remind me later.
What should the reminder say, and when would later be useful? Check the reminder tool can deliver the notification you need.
tool
Play that voice again.
Choose the voice you mean in the unwind session, then use preview or begin. A saved recording cannot identify your previous choice.
tool
I do not know whether I need rest or movement.
Notice your energy and any discomfort. You could begin with a short pause, then decide whether gentle movement appeals.
Never mind, that was not what I meant.
We can leave that idea there. Tell me what you meant in another way, without needing the perfect wording.
live
I said sleep, not a workout.
Thanks for correcting that. Choose a sleep or wind down moment so the support fits what you actually wanted.
live

title: When several things need attention
examples: I need dinner, a workout, and an early night.
Choose what needs attention first, and keep the evening realistic. You can make each part smaller or leave one for another day.
I am tired and hungry and still have work to do.
Take care of an immediate ordinary need first if you can. Then reassess how much work reasonably fits the energy left.
Can you plan my whole evening for me?
Tell me your fixed commitments and the time you have. A useful plan needs those details, with some room left open.
live
I want to calm down and then focus.
Begin with a brief settling pause. When you are ready, choose one small task instead of the whole list.
I want to exercise but also really need rest.
You can choose rest, or a very gentle amount of movement if it suits you. The decision does not need to prove anything.
I need to stop scrolling and go to bed.
Choose one ending for the scrolling, such as closing the feed. Then take the first small step of getting ready for bed.
Set a timer and add food to my shopping list.
Those are two separate app actions. Check the timer is running, then add the food items and verify the list.
tool
I have so many habits to improve that I do nothing.
Choose one area for now. Making one ordinary action easier can be enough to begin.
Can I combine a rest break with a calendar check?
You can, but it may be easier to let the rest break be a pause first. Check the calendar afterwards if you still want to.
I want the app to decide everything for me.
I can help narrow choices, but your preferences and circumstances still matter. Let's begin with just the next decision.

title: Fit the day you actually have
examples: I got home after a long train journey.
Let arriving have a little space. Put your things down somewhere safe and settle before asking anything else of yourself.
My house is busy and I cannot find quiet.
You do not need complete silence. Find the most comfortable spot available and let the surrounding sounds be part of the moment.
I have children and cannot take a long break.
Use a brief pause when it is safe and practical. Even a small moment of support can fit inside a demanding day.
I work shifts, so normal routines do not fit.
Build around your own work and rest periods. The clock on someone else's routine does not have to define yours.
I am staying away from home this week.
Choose one familiar comfort you can bring into the new place. The rest of the routine can be simpler for now.
I have very little energy today.
Make the next step smaller and include rest where you can. You do not need to use your best day as today's standard.
I am caring for someone and forgetting my own needs.
Your needs still belong in the day. Consider one practical support you could ask for, alongside a small pause for yourself.
My day changed unexpectedly.
Pause and look at what is still necessary. You can make a new, smaller plan without treating the old one as a failure.
I do not have a cosy room like the app.
You do not need a special room. A supported seat, a familiar object, or a small comfortable corner can be enough.
I just want to sit here after getting home.
Then sitting here can be the whole plan. Let yourself arrive without turning the pause into another task.

title: Leave when you are ready
examples: That is enough for today, thank you.
You can leave it there. Take whatever was useful into the rest of your day.
I feel ready to put my phone down now.
Let that be your next step. There is nothing else you need to finish in the app first.
I do not feel any different after the session.
That can happen. You have not done it wrong, and you can choose another kind of support or simply move on.
I want a little silence after this.
You can pause the audio and stay quietly. The silence does not need filling.
Can I leave halfway through a session?
Yes. Use end for now whenever you want. You do not need to reach the final second to make the visit worthwhile.
I am going to make myself some food now.
That sounds like a practical next step. Let the app wait while you take care of what you need.
I want to come back to this exercise later.
You can find the session again in Just listen. There is no need to complete another session before returning to it.
Can you end my live voice conversation?
Use the end conversation control to disconnect live voice. This saved reply cannot close the connection itself.
tool
I do not want a reminder to return.
You can visit when you choose. Review any reminders you have set if you no longer want them.
tool
Goodnight, Daywell.
Goodnight. Let the remaining tasks wait where they can. You can settle into the rest of your evening at your own pace.
